c.tagline: A Welsh-founded Patagonian coastal town, launchpad for southern right whales and penguin colonies on Peninsula Valdes

card: Widely accepted; cash (preferably USD for exchange) useful for smaller shops

taxi.fareNote: Most visitors book an organized tour rather than a taxi for Peninsula Valdes given the distances

emergency.note: 911 is the general emergency line in most of Argentina; 107 specifically reaches medical services

religion: Protestant, including a historic Welsh Chapel community (minority)
walk: The waterfront Rambla and downtown are walkable; Peninsula Valdes and Punta Tombo require a car or organized tour given the distances involved

safety.safety: Very safe city, popular as a base for Patagonian wildlife excursions

hood_landmark.Downtown: Downtown's main commercial streets around Avenida Roca

hood_desc: The scenic beachfront promenade with hotels, restaurants, and views over the Golfo Nuevo; the natural base for any visit.
The compact commercial core a short walk inland, with everyday shops, tour agencies, and dive shops.

water.note: Tap water is safe though mineral-tasting; many opt for bottled.

transit.map: Not centrally published; tour agencies handle Peninsula Valdes and Punta Tombo excursions
transit.note: A rental car or organized tour is necessary for Peninsula Valdes and Punta Tombo given the distances

transport.air: El Tehuelche Airport (PMY), about 10 min from downtown
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect to Buenos Aires (about 18-20 hr), Bariloche, and Trelew
transport.car: Rental cars available; National Route 3 connects Puerto Madryn to the rest of coastal Patagonia

net.m: Good 4G coverage in town, patchier on Peninsula Valdes
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Movistar, Claro, or Personal tourist SIM or eSIM

landmarks: Península Valdés
A UNESCO World Heritage peninsula teeming with southern right whales, orcas, elephant seals and penguins, arguably South America's finest marine-wildlife destination.
Playa El Doradillo
A pebbled beach twenty minutes from town where, between June and December, southern right whales nurse their calves just metres from shore.
Ecocentro Puerto Madryn
A striking clifftop interpretation centre celebrating Patagonian marine ecosystems, with tide-pool exhibits, art and a tower library overlooking the Golfo Nuevo.
Reserva Punta Loma
A clifftop reserve just south of the city where a noisy colony of South American sea lions lounges on the beach below year-round.
Muelle Luis Piedrabuena and the Rambla
The town's photogenic pier and seafront promenade, launch point for whale-watching seasons and sunrise strolls along the calm Golfo Nuevo.
Monumento al Indio Tehuelche
A hilltop bronze honouring the region's indigenous Tehuelche people, gazing over the bay from the spot marking the city's centenary.
Punta Tombo
A day-trip reserve hosting one of the continent's largest Magellanic penguin colonies, where hundreds of thousands of birds waddle past visitors each spring.
Puerto Pirámides
A tiny cliff-backed village inside Península Valdés, the only place in Argentina where boats depart to meet southern right whales up close.
Museo Provincial de Ciencias Naturales y Oceanográfico
Set in the elegant 1917 Chalet Pujol, this museum unravels Patagonia's marine life, from giant squid specimens to whale skeletons.
Gaiman
A day-trip-able Welsh pioneer village in the Chubut valley, famous for chapels, red dragons and traditional teahouses serving torta negra.

train.note: No railway serves Puerto Madryn - Patagonia's lines closed decades ago, apart from the narrow-gauge tourist Trochita further west. Argentina has no international passenger trains except the Posadas-Encarnación shuttle. Arrive by coach or fly into Trelew, about an hour south.

bus.note: No international coaches. The terminal in the middle of town has Andesmar (https://www.andesmar.com/) and Don Otto services to Buenos Aires in about 19 hours, Trelew in 1 and Río Gallegos down Ruta 3; local buses and tours run out to Península Valdés. Book through Plataforma 10 (https://www.plataforma10.com.ar/).

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry from Puerto Madryn - the port handles cargo and a busy cruise trade. Whale-watching boats sail from Puerto Pirámides on Península Valdés, about 100 km away, in the June-December southern right whale season, as excursions rather than transport.

half.name: Trelew
half.blurb: Welsh-founded town about an hour south holds a paleontology museum with fossils from Patagonian dinosaur excavations.

half.name: Islote Lobos
half.blurb: Protected coastal reserve about an hour north shelters sea lion colonies and nesting Magellanic penguins along a rocky shoreline.

half.name: Rawson
half.blurb: Chubut province's capital about an hour south sits at the mouth of the Chubut River, with a small fishing port and coastal cliffs.
